title: finding(app-shell): the drill URL dialect still cannot spell $exists or is_not_null, so those drills keep degrading to a superset
body:
Reported by the `os-dev` seat implementing objectui#9159 and deliberately not widened into that PR.

## The gap

objectui#9159 gave the drill `filter[...]` URL dialect an **is-null** operator, closing the silent-superset defect for `{ $null: true }`. `convertFiltersToAST` lowers three more spellings that this dialect still cannot express:

| producer spelling | lowers to | spelled in the URL dialect? |
|---|---|---|
| `{ $null: true }` | `is_null` | ✅ (objectui#9159) |
| `{ $exists: false }` | `is_null` | ⛔ no |
| `{ $null: false }` | `is_not_null` | ⛔ no |
| `{ $exists: true }` | `is_not_null` | ⛔ no |

⇒ a drill carrying one of the bottom three still **vanishes** on the escape hatch, and the list page opens scoped by everything except the condition the user clicked — the same silent-superset shape objectui#9159 measured, for the sibling spellings.

## Why it is not urgent, stated rather than assumed

`buildDatasetDrillFilter` emits `{ $null: true }` only, so **nothing on this path produces the other three today**. An authored widget filter composed into the drill (`composeDrillFilter`) can carry them, which is the reachable route.

## Why it was not fixed in place

Adding `is_not_null` doubles both the URL vocabulary and the chip vocabulary, inside what was otherwise a bug fix — and the `filter[field][null]=false` spelling was deliberately ruled NOT to be a second operator on objectui#9159, precisely so the dialect does not grow a read-side operator with no producer. Closing this needs its own write-side producer decision.

Recorded in the module's own prose as a known unspelled synonym, so the next reader of `drillUrlFilters.ts` meets it there too.

## Dedup keywords (⛔ not deduped by the filer — triage searches)

`serializeDrillFilterParams` · `$exists` · `is_not_null` · `drill URL` · `unspelled operator` · `composeDrillFilter`

## Provenance

objectui#9159 / PR objectui#9506, dev seat report. Routed unlabelled: ⛔ an execution seat does not grade or route.
